- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price movements, especially after sharp reversals.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after strong moves, assuming price will return to historical mean too quickly.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to forecast higher prices than true outcome — adjust downward by 1–2% for 30-day horizon.
- If sentiment is rising (e.g., >0.67) and price is rising, model often overestimates — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- If sentiment is falling (e.g., <0.3) and price is falling, model underestimates — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
